questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Pastoral Nomadism' refers to.
questions.a: A way of life centered on herding livestock and moving seasonally from one region to another to find fresh pastures and water.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Pastoral Nomadism'.
questions.a: Seasonal migration prevents overgrazing and allows pastures to naturally recover.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Pastoral Nomadism' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1. Pastoral Nomads and their Movements (source: iess305.txt lines 12-40)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Mountain Pastoralists of India' refers to.
questions.a: Herding communities in the Himalayan region, such as Gujjar Bakarwals and Gaddis, who migrate between low-altitude winter scrub forests and high-altitude summer meadows.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Mountain Pastoralists of India'.
questions.a: Migration is dictated by snowmelt in summer and freezing temperatures in winter.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Mountain Pastoralists of India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.1 In the Mountains (source: iess305.txt lines 41-110)

concepts.title: Plateau and Desert Pastoralists of India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Plateau and Desert Pastoralists of India' refers to.
questions.a: Pastoral groups like Dhangars, Gollas, Kurubas, Banjaras, and Raikas whose seasonal movements are shaped by monsoon cycles rather than cold or snow.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Plateau and Desert Pastoralists of India'.
questions.a: Alternation between dry inland plateaus or deserts during monsoons and wet coastal or riverine tracts in dry seasons.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Plateau and Desert Pastoralists of India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.2 On the Plateaus, Plains and Deserts (source: iess305.txt lines 111-180)

concepts.title: Colonial Forest Acts and Pastoral Impact

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Colonial Forest Acts and Pastoral Impact' refers to.
questions.a: Laws enacted by the British administration classifying forests into Reserved and Protected categories, severely restricting pastoralists' access to grazing land.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Colonial Forest Acts and Pastoral Impact'.
questions.a: Forest reservation protected commercial timber but deprived herders of traditional grazing rights.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Colonial Forest Acts and Pastoral Impact' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2. Colonial Rule and Pastoral Life (source: iess305.txt lines 220-265)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Waste Land Rules' refers to.
questions.a: Mid-nineteenth-century colonial regulations aimed at converting uncultivated grazing lands into revenue-generating agricultural fields.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Waste Land Rules'.
questions.a: Colonial state viewed uncultivated land as unproductive waste because it yielded no land revenue.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Waste Land Rules' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2. Colonial Rule and Pastoral Life (source: iess305.txt lines 195-219)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Criminal Tribes Act' refers to.
questions.a: An 1871 British legislative act that classified nomadic communities, including herders and mobile traders, as criminal by birth and restricted them to fixed settlements.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Criminal Tribes Act'.
questions.a: Colonial preference for a settled, easily taxable, and controllable population over mobile groups.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Criminal Tribes Act' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2. Colonial Rule and Pastoral Life (source: iess305.txt lines 266-285)

questions.q: Calculate the total grazing tax paid by a herder.. Use the method 'Grazing Tax Calculation'. Work with: cattle_count = 30, tax_per_head = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_tax.
questions.a: 540 units

questions.q: Find the total grazing tax given the tax per animal and the number of cattle.. Use the method 'Grazing Tax Calculation'. Work with: cattle_count = 120, tax_per_head = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_tax.
questions.a: 3000 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Grazing Tax Calculation' refers to.
questions.a: A colonial tax levied on pastoralists for every head of cattle or animal they grazed on public pastures.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Grazing Tax Calculation'.
questions.a: Maximizing state revenue by taxing the livestock of nomadic herders.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Grazing Tax Calculation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_tax = tax_per_head * cattle_count

questions.q: Calculate the remaining land area of the Maasai after losing a percentage of their territory.. Use the method 'Maasai Land Area After Loss'. Work with: original_land = 250, percent_lost = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of remaining_land.
questions.a: 205 sq units

questions.q: Find the area of land left with the Maasai herders.. Use the method 'Maasai Land Area After Loss'. Work with: original_land = 1200, percent_lost = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of remaining_land.
questions.a: 1056 sq units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Maasai Land Area After Loss' refers to.
questions.a: The calculation of remaining grazing land after colonial boundaries and white settlements alienated a percentage of the original Maasai territory.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Maasai Land Area After Loss'.
questions.a: Colonial partition and game reserves reduced Maasai grazing lands by a specific percentage (typically 60%).

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Maasai Land Area After Loss', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: remaining_land = original_land * (100 - percent_lost) / 100

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Social Stratification in Maasai Society' refers to.
questions.a: The division of Maasai society into elders and warriors in pre-colonial times, which was disrupted by British administrative policies appointing chiefs and creating wealth disparities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Social Stratification in Maasai Society'.
questions.a: Colonial rule weakened traditional age-based authority and introduced a new class divide between rich and poor pastoralists.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Social Stratification in Maasai Society' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.4 Not All were Equally Affected (source: iess305.txt lines 460-520)
